o.text: Borrowed from Russian кло́ун (klóun), from English clown.
From Arabic سَلَامَات (salāmāt), plural of سَلَامَة (salāma, “good health”).
Borrowed from Russian алмаз (almaz), from Tatar алмаз (almaz), from Persian الماس (almâs, “diamond”).
Morphologically from ov (“hunt”) + -çu. Cognate with Turkish avcı, Uzbek ovchi, Old Turkic [script needed] (avčï, “hunter”).
Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *ebi-s-. Cognate with Turkish esmek, Southern Altai эс- (es-), etc.
From atatürkçü + -lük. Calque of Turkish Atatürkçülük.
